subtitle: To-dos kept on your own server
promotionalText: Your lists and tasks, kept in the substrate you run, and on every device you sign in to.
description:
Substrate Tasks is a to-do list that lives in your substrate, the personal server you run or choose. Your lists and tasks are records on that server, so they stay yours: there is no account with us, and your tasks go to your server and nowhere else.

• Tasks with a due day or a due time, and a priority
• Lists in the order you choose
• Reminders when a task is due, once you turn them on
• Works offline: changes wait on your device and are sent when you are back online
• Updates live when something changes on your server
• On iPhone and iPad

Substrate Tasks is a client for a substrate. Sign in with your server's address and approve what the app may do there: it asks to keep your lists and tasks, and to see which other collections on your server could be shown as tasks. It changes one of those only after you turn it on and approve that too.
reviewNotes:
Substrate Tasks is a to-do list for people who keep their data on Substrate, a personal server they run or choose. We run a demonstration server for review, with no real user's data.

To sign in:
1. Open the app. Under Repository or server, enter {server} and tap Continue.
2. iOS asks whether Tasks may use that server to sign in: tap Continue. The server's sign-in page opens by itself. If you close it, tap Sign In with Your Substrate to open it again.
3. On the Sign in to your Substrate page, enter the name and password below and tap Sign in.
4. Scroll down and tap Approve and set up. The button reads Approve or Keep access once the app has been set up on the server. The app returns signed in.

Name: {user}
Password: {password}

Then create a list and a few tasks. Reminders are off until you turn them on in Settings, which is when the app asks to send notifications.

Accounts: the app creates no account and holds none. A person's account is on their own server, made there by its operator's invitation. The sign-in page's Create your Substrate link belongs to the server and needs an invite code, which the app does not give. The owner deletes the account and everything in it on the server: Settings, Delete your Substrate. Signing out of the app revokes the app's access on the server.

Updates: the app has no updater. It does not look for, download, install or run code, and Settings shows its version and nothing to check. Privacy policy: {privacy}
